processed.title: Association of non-methane volatile organic compound emission burden with chronic kidney disease: integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic and in vitro analyses.

figures.label: Figure 1.
figures.caption: Spatial distribution of province-level NMVOC emission burden and its association with the odds of prevalent CKD. (A) Spatial geographic distribution map of CKD prevalence across regions. The color intensity represents the level of prevalence or exposure. (B) Multivariate logistic regression model evaluating the association between province-level NMVOC emission burden and CKD risk. (C-F) Stratified subgroup analyses of the association between province-level NMVOC emission burden and CKD according to (C) obesity status, (D) lipid status, (E) smoking status, and (F) alcohol consumption status. Model 1: Unadjusted; Model 2: Adjusted for age, gender, BMI, place of residence, educational level, and marital status; Model 3: Further adjusted for smoking, alcohol consumption, TG, HDL, LDL, CRP, SBP, and DBP based on Model 2.

figures.label: Figure 2.
figures.caption: Identification of core targets and functional enrichment analysis of province-level NMVOC emission burden driving CKD development. (A) Venn diagram illustrating the intersection between the targets of main NMVOC components (formaldehyde, benzene, isoprene, and trichloroethylene) and CKD-related genes. (B) Bar chart of Gene Ontology (GO) functional enrichment analysis for the intersecting targets. (C) Bar chart of KEGG pathway enrichment analysis for the intersecting targets.

figures.label: Figure 3.
figures.caption: Comprehensive regulatory network and screening of core hub genes. (A) Network diagram constructed using Cytoscape, illustrating the regulation of CKD by the main exposure components of NMVOCs via 165 intersecting targets. Node size and color represent their topological importance (Degree value) within the network. (B) The top 10 key hub genes screened through network topological analysis.

figures.label: Figure 4.
figures.caption: Construction of machine learning diagnostic models and evaluation of core feature genes based on SHAP analysis. (A) Heatmap of the top 10 machine learning algorithm combinations based on their comprehensive performance (AUC values) in the training set (GSE37171) and the external validation set (GSE66494). (B-E) SHAP visualization analysis of the optimal model, including a bar plot (B), beeswarm plot (C), force plot (D), and waterfall plot (E), demonstrating the contributions and weights of the core genes to the model predictions. (F) Single-gene ROC curves of the core feature genes in the independent validation, evaluating their individual diagnostic efficacy.

figures.label: Figure 5.
figures.caption: Validation of the differential expression of the 5 core feature genes in external transcriptome cohorts.

figures.label: Figure 6.
figures.caption: Single-cell analysis and virtual knockout-based investigation of SLC9A3-associated microenvironmental signaling in CKD. (A) UMAP dimensionality reduction clustering plot of the global cell landscape in human healthy control and CKD kidney samples, identifying a total of 10 major cell subpopulations. (B) Highly specific expression enrichment of the SLC9A3 gene in proximal tubular cells. (C) Signaling pathway analysis within the CKD microenvironment, showing significant enrichment of the SPP1 pathway. (D) Cell communication analysis demonstrating the targeted interaction between the SPP1 ligand secreted by proximal tubular cells and the integrin receptor complex (ITGAV+ITGB1) on the surface of fibroblasts. (E,F) Directional analysis of predicted pathway activities and compensatory expression changes following targeted perturbation of the SPP1 signaling axis receptors.

figures.label: Figure 7.
figures.caption: In vitro proof-of-concept assessment of tubular and fibroblast responses in a hydroquinone model. (A) Viability of NRK-52E cells treated with 0, 10, or 20 μmol/L hydroquinone (HQ) for the indicated periods. (B) Relative SLC9A3 and SPP1 mRNA expression in NRK-52E cells after 24 h of HQ treatment. (C-D) Representative Western blots and densitometric quantification of SLC9A3 and SPP1 protein expression in NRK-52E cells. GAPDH served as the loading control. (E-F) Representative Western blots and densitometric quantification of ITGB1 and α-SMA expression in NRK-49F cells assigned to the FBS-only, CM-Control, CM-HQ10, CM-HQ20, Direct-HQ10, and Direct-HQ20 groups. (G-H) Representative Transwell images and quantitative analysis of migrated NRK-49F cells in the six experimental groups. Scale bars, 200μm. FBS-only denotes fresh complete medium containing 10% FBS without HQ or conditioned medium. CM-Control denotes conditioned medium collected from control NRK-52E cells. CM-HQ10 and CM-HQ20 denote conditioned medium collected after HQ removal and washout from NRK-52E cells previously exposed to 10 or 20 μmol/L HQ, respectively. Direct-HQ10 and Direct-HQ20 denote fresh complete medium containing the corresponding HQ concentration without conditioned medium. ns, P ≥ 0.05; *** P < 0.001.

processed.title: Customized MUC1 Sequencing Enables Diagnosis of Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease and Unexplained CKD.

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Comparative coverage of the MUC1- VNTR region between WES and the customized HTS panel. (a) Read alignment from WES mapped against the VNTR region. (b) Read alignment from customized NGS mapped against the VNTR region. NGS, next-generation sequencing.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Visualization of the c.428dup (DupC) variant using the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV and Sanger sequencing electropherograms. The IGV alignments enable reliable detection of the DupC variant when located within the first VNTR module, owing to the high mappability of this region. The variant is also identified by the variant-calling pipeline with an alternative allele frequency within the expected range for a heterozygous variant. The presence of the DupC variant was confirmed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing, as illustrated in the electropherogram, where a characteristic double peak is observed at the insertion site.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Graphical representation of the relationship between mutant allele read frequency and sequencing depth among 550 patients for the NC_000001.10:g.(155160963_155162030)insG variant. Red circles represent true-positive cases for the DupC variant. Black circles indicate true-negative cases. Blue circles represent negative cases without secondary confirmation, observed in most individuals. The red dashed line denotes the positive zone with high sensitivity (ratio ≥ 0.5), whereas the blue dashed lines define the zone of uncertainty (ratio 0.36–0.54). The orange line depicts the threshold (0.45) of variant frequency to consider a potential positive variant, which should be confirmed.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Phasing analysis and alignment of LRS in 4 samples positive for the DupC variant in the MUC1 gene. (a) Graphical representation of the number of reads containing VNTR modules, distinguishing both alleles. Wild-type modules are represented in green; slight differences (< 90%) from the consensus module are represented in blue; MUC1 -frameshift variants are represented in orange; and the target mutation (DupC) is represented in red. DupC is aligned in the same repeats on the affected allele. (b) Number of repeats and location for each sample.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Graphical representation of the relationship between mutant allele read frequency and sequencing depth among 550 patients for the NC_000001.10:g.(155160963_155162030)insT variant. Red circles represent true-positive cases for the DupA variant. Black circles indicate true-negative cases. Blue circles represent negative cases without secondary confirmation, observed in most individuals. Orange circles represent patients from the same family.
